name: i9 Monitoramento de Cliques
author: i9 Publicidade

sections.description:
i9 Monitoramento de Cliques automatically tracks and analyzes user interactions with buttons, links, PDF files, WhatsApp links, and forms directly on your WordPress site.

Built with a strong focus on performance, privacy, and compliance with LGPD, GDPR, and WordPress.org Directory guidelines:

  • 100% Local Data & Privacy: No data is transmitted to external servers. All interaction records remain strictly within your local WordPress database.
  • Strict Prior Consent by Default (Guideline 7): When activated, prior consent for statistics is strictly required by default before any tracking scripts record events or store client tokens. Native compatibility with WP Consent API, Complianz, Cookiebot, and Klaro.
  • Zero Storage Before Consent: Technical pseudonymous session identifiers (localStorage and sessionStorage) are never read or stored until visitor consent is granted, and are immediately purged if consent is revoked.
  • No Plaintext IP Storage: Does not store plaintext IP addresses or Personally Identifiable Information (PII) in permanent tables.
  • Built-in Analytics Dashboard: Monitor daily trends, peak engagement hours, button rankings, and estimated unique visitors.
  • Native PDF Reports: Generates executive and comprehensive A4 PDF reports directly in PHP without heavy third-party dependencies. Customize brand name and header logo from the admin panel.
  • Secure CSV Exports: Export aggregated metrics or full historical logs with native protection against CSV formula injection.
  • Block Editor & Page Builder Friendly: Works seamlessly with the Gutenberg Block Editor and popular page builders like Elementor.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the i9-monitoramento-de-cliques directory to /wp-content/plugins/ or upload the .zip file via Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen in WordPress.
  3. Navigate to i9 Cliques in the WordPress admin menu to view analytics and adjust settings.
sections.faq:
Does the plugin send data to external third-party servers?

No. All data processing and storage happens locally in your own WordPress database. No analytics data is shared with external SaaS platforms.

Does the plugin store IP addresses or personal data?

No. The plugin is built with privacy-by-design principles. It never stores plaintext IP addresses, user form submissions, or personal information. It uses technical pseudonymous identifiers generated in the browser to estimate sessions and visitors only after consent is granted.

How does consent work?

By default upon activation, prior consent for statistics is required (require_consent = 1). The tracking script automatically integrates with WP Consent API, Complianz, Cookiebot, and Klaro. If consent is granted, tracking activates; if consent is declined or revoked, all identifiers are purged and zero events are sent. If your website operates in an environment where anonymous first-party analytics do not require a cookie banner, you may toggle off “Exigir consentimento prévio” in Settings.

What happens to data when the plugin is uninstalled?

By default, to prevent accidental data loss during plugin updates or temporary reinstalls, the database table and historical logs are preserved. If you wish to permanently wipe all database tables and records on uninstall, enable the “Excluir dados ao desinstalar” setting in Settings before deleting the plugin.

How can I customize the logo and brand name on PDF reports?

Go to i9 Cliques > Configurações. Under Identidade dos relatórios PDF, enter your company or organization name and select an image from your WordPress Media Library.

How do I exclude a specific button from tracking?

In the Gutenberg Block Editor, select the button block and add the CSS class smc-ignore under Advanced > Additional CSS class(es). If writing custom HTML, add the attribute data-smc-ignore="1" to the element.

Is it compatible with Elementor?

Yes. The tracking script recognizes links and buttons generated by standard WordPress core blocks as well as Elementor button widgets.
sections.changelog:
2.3.21

  • Fix: Automatically refresh WordPress rewrite rules after plugin installation or update.
  • Fix: Addressed an issue where click tracking could require manually saving Permalink Settings.
  • Improvement: Refresh rewrite rules only when necessary to avoid unnecessary processing.

2.3.20

  • Compliance: Updated display name to ‘i9 Monitoramento de Cliques’ and slug/text domain to ‘i9-monitoramento-de-cliques’ per WordPress.org review.
  • Privacy (Guideline 7): Prior consent is strictly enabled by default on clean installations, ensuring zero events and zero local storage before visitor consent.
  • Privacy: Added automated identity cleanup upon consent revocation events.
  • Code Quality: Removed all inline <script> tags from admin HTML templates; enqueued admin logic cleanly via wp_enqueue_script with scoped assets/admin.js.
  • Security & Naming: Standardized internal transient keys and scheduled cron hooks with distinct 4+ character prefixes (i9mc_).
  • Retrocompatibility: Full backward compatibility preserved for existing database tables (wp_salvata_cliques), legacy options (smc_options), and legacy REST routes.

2.3.19

  • Enhanced REST API security with Origin/Referer validation and dual rate-limiting (per visitor session and per IP hash).
  • Standardized primary REST route /monitoramento-cliques/v1/event while maintaining legacy route backward compatibility.
  • Optional prior consent toggle for full LGPD/GDPR compliance with WP Consent API and Complianz integration.
  • Added explicit option to preserve or wipe data on uninstallation, preventing accidental history loss.
  • Updated readme.txt to meet official WordPress.org guidelines with English documentation.

2.3.18

  • Added Estimated Visitors card (distinct pseudonymous visitor count) to the dashboard overview.

2.3.17

  • Added Website Visits (Sessions) and Pageview indicators directly to the dashboard overview.

2.3.16

  • WordPress.org repository compliance updates.
  • Refactored PDF generation to native GD image processing, removing proprietary binary assets.
  • Full internationalization (i18n) across all administrative screens.
  • Strict REST API parameter sanitization and CSV injection prevention.
  • Added uninstall.php with administrative deletion safeguards.

2.3.15

  • Refactored settings interface into independent panels.
